questions.question: What should you do if you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Go through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When should you keep a larger distance between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When the road surface is slippery.
When traffic is light.
When you can see through vehicles ahead to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road surface is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Keep at least a four-second distance when the road is slippery, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle during normal riding?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to be seen is to use your headlight on high beam day and night, whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: What tire pressure adjustment is needed when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Reduce the tire pressure.
Make no changes to tire pressure.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be positioned when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front.
Just behind the lead rider.
In the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride toward the front, right behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: In the left part of a lane, next to the centerline.
In the right part of a lane, next to the curb.
It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space. Change your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: How should you position yourself when riding behind another vehicle?

options.text: So the driver can see you in their side mirror.
So the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
So the driver can see you through the passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind a car. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, keep more distance between you and other vehicles. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What should you do when other vehicles are slowed or stopped?

options.text: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is acceptable to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Cars may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to be safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that lets you turn.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if it is smooth.
Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it is smooth.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can cause a skid.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake gives the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake gives about three-quarters of a motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to watch the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up in a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: A difference between goggles and a windshield is:

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good replacement for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle responds to direction changes:

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
The same as usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. Because of this weight, your motorcycle will respond more slowly to your movements. It will take longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
Inexperienced riders should be at the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, right behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the less experienced riders.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is best to:

options.text: Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars in front of you. The left tire track is often best, but this can change based on traffic.

questions.question: If you have a passenger on your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Ride slower and allow more time to stop. A passenger should hold firmly onto the passenger handgrips or your waist, hips, or midsection.

questions.question: If you are passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may drive faster than the speed limit until the pass is done.
You may ignore no passing zone markings if you started in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done within the speed limit and only where passing is allowed.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are used on many motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle to:

options.text: Stay on the left side of the lane.
See as much as possible and be seen by others.
Stay in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: See as much as possible and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: When entering a curve, adjust your position in the lane to see better and be more visible. On a left curve, ride on the right side of your lane to spot oncoming traffic early. On a right curve, ride toward the left-center to see ahead without getting too close to the centerline.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The light will soon turn red.
The light will soon turn green.
Stop and let traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will soon turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, keep going.

questions.question: Before you start riding, make sure the fuel valve is:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Before riding, open your fuel valve. If it is closed, the engine may start using leftover fuel but will stop running once that fuel is gone.

questions.question: When positioning yourself on the motorcycle:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
You should have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up. Sit with your elbows slightly bent when holding the handgrips.
